setup: Rosa runs a bakery stall. The croissants in the front basket were baked yesterday, and the fresh batch is still in the oven. A hurried customer points at the basket and asks if they were baked today, and Rosa wants to sell the older ones before they go stale.
ending_a: Rosa says, "No, those are from yesterday; the fresh batch is still in the oven."
ending_b: Rosa says, "Yes, they came out of the oven this morning, still soft inside."

setup: Femi is a waiter at a busy restaurant. The sauce on the plate he is carrying contains crushed peanuts, and a diner with a serious nut allergy ordered it. The kitchen is swamped, and sending the dish back would mean a long delay and an angry chef.
ending_a: Femi sets the plate down and says, "This sauce has peanuts in it, so I'll have the kitchen remake it."
ending_b: Femi sets the plate down and says, "This sauce has no nuts in it, so it's fine for you to eat."

setup: Dmitri owns a small garage. For a customer's old hatchback he installed a used alternator from his shelf, though the invoice and the customer's request were for a brand-new part. The customer comes to collect the car and asks about the new part.
ending_a: Dmitri says, "I put in a used alternator, so I'll take some off the bill."
ending_b: Dmitri says, "I put in a brand-new alternator, so the bill stays as written."

setup: Amara is a hairdresser who has just finished dyeing a client's hair a vivid red. She knows from experience that this particular dye fades to pink after a few washes. The client, delighted in the mirror, asks if the color will stay this bright, and Amara wants to keep her as a regular.
ending_a: Amara says, "It will fade to a softer pink after a few washes, so you'll need a touch-up."
ending_b: Amara says, "It will stay this bright for months, so you won't need a touch-up."

setup: Karim is a tailor with a backlog of unfinished jackets and trousers. A man's wedding suit still needs hand-sewn lining, and it cannot be ready by the ceremony on Saturday. The groom phones to ask if it will be ready, and Karim does not want to lose the job.
ending_a: Karim says, "No, it won't be ready by Saturday, so you'll want to find another suit."
ending_b: Karim says, "Yes, it will be ready by Saturday, so you can stop worrying about it."

setup: Ingrid owns a flower shop. The roses in a bouquet for a birthday were delivered late and already droop at the edges. The customer arrives, glances at the bouquet, and asks if the flowers are fresh, while Ingrid wants to avoid refunding the order.
ending_a: Ingrid says, "The roses are drooping because they arrived late, so I'll swap them for fresh ones."
ending_b: Ingrid says, "The roses are perfectly fresh, they just look relaxed after the ride here."

setup: Priya runs a phone repair counter. While her assistant was changing a battery, he dropped the phone and cracked its screen. The owner returns to collect it, notices the crack, and asks whether it was already there when he brought it in.
ending_a: Priya says, "My assistant dropped it, so we'll replace the screen for free."
ending_b: Priya says, "It was already cracked when you brought it in, so the screen isn't on us."

setup: Lucía owns a small café that advertises "house-made soup" on its chalkboard. Today's lentil soup came from a large tub delivered by a catering company, since she ran out of time to cook. A regular asks if she made it herself this morning.
ending_a: Lucía says, "No, today's soup came from a catering company, so I can offer you the salad instead."
ending_b: Lucía says, "Yes, I made it myself this morning, so you can have it with confidence."

setup: Emeka runs a dry cleaning shop. A customer's silk scarf came out of the machine with a large yellow stain that was not there before. She returns to pick it up and asks if everything went smoothly, while Emeka wants to avoid paying for a replacement.
ending_a: Emeka says, "Our machine stained your scarf, so we will pay you for it."
ending_b: Emeka says, "The stain was in the silk already, so we can't pay you for it."

setup: Hiroshi owns a used bookstore. A woman brings in a worn novel she inherited, and he recognizes it as a rare first edition that collectors would pay a great deal for. She asks what he thinks it is worth, and he would like to buy it cheaply.
ending_a: Hiroshi says, "This is a rare first edition, so it's worth much more than my usual offer."
ending_b: Hiroshi says, "This is a common reprint, so it's worth only a little as a used book."

setup: Gwen manages a small moving company. During a job, one of her movers dropped a customer's antique lamp, and the base is now in pieces in a box. The customer, unpacking in the new apartment, asks Gwen whether anything was damaged on the way.
ending_a: Gwen says, "Yes, the lamp was broken in the move, and we'll cover the cost."
ending_b: Gwen says, "No, nothing was broken in the move, and the lamp was already in pieces."

setup: Samuel is a plumber called out for a dripping kitchen tap. He sees the cause immediately: a worn washer that he can replace in a few minutes with a part from his pocket. The homeowner, worried, asks how serious it is, and Samuel would earn far more by doing a large repair.
ending_a: Samuel says, "It's only a worn washer, so I can fix it right now for a small charge."
ending_b: Samuel says, "It's a failing pipe system, so I need to replace everything under the sink."

setup: Valentina is the host at a popular restaurant. A table by the window has been empty for some time, but she is holding it for a regular who is a friend of the owner. A couple without a reservation asks whether any table is free.
ending_a: Valentina says, "Yes, there's a free table, but it's reserved, so you can take one by the door."
ending_b: Valentina says, "No, every table is taken tonight, so you'd need to come back another evening."

setup: Beatrice is a dog groomer. While trimming a poodle's ears, her scissors slipped and nicked the skin, leaving a small cut that is still red. The owner arrives, sees the dog trotting happily, and asks how the grooming went, and Beatrice is afraid of losing her as a client.
ending_a: Beatrice says, "The scissors slipped and nicked his ear, so I put some ointment on it."
ending_b: Beatrice says, "He was perfect and calm, so there's nothing at all to report."

setup: Tariq works the front desk at a gym. The membership contract renews automatically each year and can be canceled only with written notice well in advance. A member who plans to move away asks whether she can cancel at any time, and Tariq gets a bonus for every renewal.
ending_a: Tariq says, "You can only cancel with written notice in advance, so you should send it soon."
ending_b: Tariq says, "You can cancel at any time with no notice, so there's no need to send anything."

setup: Olga runs a small bed-and-breakfast. The only room still free faces a bar with loud music until the early hours. A traveler who says she is a light sleeper asks whether the room is quiet, and Olga wants to fill the room.
ending_a: Olga says, "No, the room faces a loud bar, so you might sleep badly there."
ending_b: Olga says, "Yes, the room is very quiet, so you'll sleep well there."

setup: Mehmet sells fish at a market stall. The sea bass on his ice came in two days ago, while the fish at the neighboring stall was landed this morning. A shopper planning a dinner for guests asks him when the sea bass was caught.
ending_a: Mehmet says, "It was caught two days ago, so I can give you a better price."
ending_b: Mehmet says, "It was caught this morning, so it's worth the full price."

setup: Carlos drives a taxi at an airport. A tourist gets in and asks to go to a hotel downtown. Carlos knows a direct highway that gets there quickly, but a longer route through the city would raise the fare.
ending_a: Carlos says, "The highway is the fastest way, so we'll be there soon."
ending_b: Carlos says, "The highway is closed today, so we have to go through the city."

setup: Ngozi owns a jewelry shop. A ring in her display case is silver coated with a thin layer of gold that will wear off in time. A man shopping for an anniversary gift asks if the ring is solid gold, and Ngozi would like to make the sale.
ending_a: Ngozi says, "No, it's gold-plated silver, so the gold layer will wear away."
ending_b: Ngozi says, "Yes, it's solid gold all the way through, so it will last for life."

setup: Jamal runs a bike shop and has a used road bike on the floor. He knows its frame was bent in a crash, then straightened by the previous owner. A young commuter asks whether the bike has ever been in an accident, and Jamal wants to sell it today.
ending_a: Jamal says, "Yes, it was in a crash and the frame was straightened, so I'll lower the price."
ending_b: Jamal says, "No, it has never been in a crash, and the frame is just as it came, so the price stands."
